name: Shiloh
overview: Shiloh is a significant location in Israelite history, serving as the site where the tabernacle was established and the congregation of Israel assembled during the time of Joshua, marking it as a central place of worship and governance (Joshua 18:1). It functioned as a gathering place for the tribes and a seat of leadership, underscored by the assembly of the Levite heads and the people of Israel (Joshua 21:1-2). The city also witnessed important events such as the departure of certain tribes to their allotted lands and the congregation's readiness to respond to conflict (Joshua 22:9, 12). Additionally, Shiloh carries messianic significance as a name of Jesus, symbolizing the coming ruler to whom the gathering of the people belongs (Genesis 49:10).
